brief.headline: Memory selloff deepens—SK Hynix ADR whipsaws, Samsung earnings disappoint; HBM structural story intact but profit-taking dominates flow
brief.summary: <cite index="46-7,46-9">Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix, and the Roundhill Memory ETF are all down more than 20% from recent closing highs, despite Samsung's operating profit estimate of $59 billion and sales of $113 billion.</cite> <cite index="43-1,43-12">SK Hynix's Nasdaq ADR debut whipsawed from a 27% surge Tuesday to a 5% drop Wednesday, reflecting a thin float, ADR premium to Seoul-listed shares, and heavy demand from newly launched leveraged products.</cite> <cite index="10-2,16-13,16-14">DRAM contract prices are expected to rise 20–30% in Q3 2026, with NAND prices climbing 35–40%, driven by AI-driven demand that continues to starve consumer supply and shift capacity to HBM and enterprise SSDs.</cite> <cite index="19-1,19-15">The four largest US hyperscalers are guiding to roughly $725 billion in combined 2026 capex, up 77% from approximately $410 billion in 2025.</cite> <cite index="30-10">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from around 20% currently to about 10% by end-2026.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="3-11,3-12">SK Hynix maintains a dominant position with a 62% share of HBM shipments as of Q2 2025 and 57% of revenue as of Q3, with Goldman Sachs assessing the company will maintain over 50% total HBM market share through at least 2026.</cite> <cite index="3-17">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in the HBM4 market for Nvidia's next-generation Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="40-8">Samsung held a 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus SK Hynix's 53%, though customers have stated 'Samsung is back' on HBM4.</cite> <cite index="4-9,4-10">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers in June 2026 on schedule, leveraging advanced HBM development and production expertise.</cite> Long SK Hynix versus Samsung—SK's execution lead on HBM4/4E ramp, packaging partnership with TSMC, and 70% Rubin share projection justify the premium. Samsung's HBM4 qualification progress is real but trailing by 2–3 quarters. ADR volatility creates entry windows; Seoul-listed 000660.KS offers tighter liquidity. Relative multiple compression on Samsung (trading ~8x NTM EV/EBITDA vs SK Hynix ~12x) reflects structural HBM share gap, not valuation opportunity.

memory_cycle.stage: Late upcycle with demand-side acceleration outpacing supply response
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-10">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93–98% quarter-over-quarter in Q1 2026, with buyers signing fresh contracts paying roughly double what they paid three months earlier.</cite> <cite index="14-7,14-8">Q2 2026 saw DRAM contract prices rise 58–63% QoQ and NAND Flash prices jump 70–75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90–95% DRAM increase.</cite> <cite index="15-22,15-25">Hyperscaler capex among the top eight cloud providers is projected to exceed $600 billion in 2026, a 40% YoY increase, with HBM consuming wafer capacity at a 3-to-1 conversion ratio versus DDR5.</cite> <cite index="13-17">Meaningful new NAND supply is not expected until late 2027 or 2028.</cite> Pricing power remains with suppliers through at least Q4 2026; consumer demand destruction is real (smartphone shipments down 14% in 2026) but enterprise AI pull dominates. HBM allocation tightness supports conventional DRAM/NAND ASPs via capacity cannibalization. First signs of buyer fatigue visible in spot market behavior, but contract pricing momentum intact.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-7,3-9">HBM3E is expected to remain the flagship product in the 2026 HBM market, accounting for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments, while HBM4 gradually increases its share.</cite> <cite index="5-11">Nvidia has reportedly asked major memory suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026, though discussions remain exploratory with no contracts signed.</cite> <cite index="6-2,6-12">Samsung and SK Hynix are prioritizing ramping HBM4 production, keeping HBM3E supply tight and continuing to lag demand.</cite> <cite index="7-20">TSMC's CoWoS is moving toward CoWoS-L, enabling up to 12 HBM3E/HBM4 stacks for 2026 AI parts, with a larger A16 generation planned for 2027.</cite> <cite index="5-21">SK Hynix has already established an HBM4 mass production framework and has been supplying paid samples to Nvidia.</cite> Nvidia's 16-layer inquiry accelerates generational transition timeline, pulling forward HBM4E even before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout. SK Hynix's June HBM4E sample shipment (48GB, 16Gbps, 20%+ power efficiency gain) positions it 2–3 quarters ahead of Samsung on next-gen ramp. Pricing tailwind persists: HBM3E reportedly saw ~20% ASP hikes for 2026 contracts amid H200 China export approval and hyperscaler ASIC adoption (Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium3).

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers on schedule (June 18, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: Confirms SK's execution lead on next-gen HBM. 48GB capacity, 16Gbps speed, 20%+ power efficiency gain vs HBM4. Leverages Advanced MR-MUF for 12-layer structural stability. Mass production timing TBD but ahead of Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as capacity expands (June 15, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing faster than expected. TSMC capacity targeting 115–140k wpm by end-2026, up from 13k in 2023. Reduces packaging gating factor for HBM4 ramp in 2H26. Positive for both SK Hynix (TSMC packaging partnership) and Samsung (SiP alternative urgency declines).

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns DRAM prices +20–30%, NAND +35–40% in Q3 2026 as AI starves consumer supply
news_pulse.implication: Q3 pricing momentum intact despite consumer demand destruction. Allocation to HBM/enterprise SSDs continues to compress client supply. ADATA seeing 212% YoY revenue growth driven by price, not volume. Shortages expected through 2028 unless new fabs come online faster.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725B, nearly double mid-2025 estimates (May 2026)
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Microsoft $190B, Google $175–185B, Meta $115–135B. ~75% allocated to AI infrastructure (GPUs, HBM, servers, networking). Consensus was $365B one year ago—estimates doubling in 12 months. Capex rising faster than operating cash flow, driving debt issuance, but AI memory demand structural.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 7–9% as chip rout spreads from Nasdaq (July 2, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after parabolic YTD runs. Nasdaq weakness spilled into Asia. SK Hynix CEO announced $64B South Korea investment (M17 NAND fab, P&T7 packaging). Fundamentals unchanged but positioning extended. ADR debut timing unfortunate—thin float exacerbates volatility.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ADR debut on Nasdaq whipsaws: +27% Tuesday, -5% Wednesday (July 10–15, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: Thin float, ADR premium to Seoul shares, and leveraged ETF demand create extreme volatility. Put/call ratio at 1.12 vs Micron's 0.91. Bull case intact (HBM dominance, structural AI upcycle) but post-debut technical overhang. Seoul-listed 000660.KS offers better execution for institutionals.

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix down 20%+ from recent highs (July 7, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: Samsung's record profit ($59B operating profit, $113B sales) failed to satisfy. Semiconductor basket lost $1.5T market cap since June 25. Micron down $350B, Sandisk/Intel/AMAT/LRCX each down $100B+. Structural shortage story vs. peak-pricing debate. Sentiment inflection, not fundamental inflection.

news_pulse.headline: South Korea unveils $518B semiconductor mega-project: Samsung, SK Hynix each building 2 new fabs (June 29, 2026)
news_pulse.implication: 800 trillion won national ecosystem project. Samsung also announced separate $646B decade-long blueprint (300T won for new fabs, 360T for Yongin cluster, 350T for AI data centers). SK Hynix M15X fab operational by mid-2027, Samsung P5 by 2028. Supply response materializing but 18–24 months out. Shares sold off on announcement—'buy the rumor, sell the news' dynamic.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="43-7,43-8">SK Hynix ADR put/call ratio sits at 1.12 across the full chain, while Micron sits at 0.91, with options positioning tilting slightly defensive.</cite> Kospi futures gapped down hard early July, recovered intraday but closed weak. Leveraged ETFs linked to Samsung/SK Hynix (newly launched in Korea) all trading below 20,000 won listing price after underlying stocks dropped 6%+. Implied vol elevated but not panic levels—VIX equivalent for memory names at 35–40 range vs 25 prior. Flow suggests tactical de-risking rather than structural unwind. Near-term resistance at Seoul highs (Samsung 330k, SK Hynix 2.5M); support at 200-day MA (Samsung 270k, SK Hynix 2.0M). ADR premium to Seoul shares compressed from 8% to 2% post-debut—arbitrage window closing.

Any Nvidia commentary on HBM4 qualification timing or 16-layer HBM requirements for Rubin
KOSPI tech sector flow—foreign selling vs domestic 'Ants' dip-buying behavior
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for DDR5/HBM3E (contract pricing lags but spot leads sentiment)
CoWoS supply chain chatter—any TSMC packaging allocation shifts favoring Samsung vs SK Hynix would be material
